profile.summary: This is the in silico VHH, or nanobody, design comparison published with TorchCraft. Fifteen protein targets, each with a PDB entry, a crop and hotspot residues in Supplementary Table S5, are designed against by four methods, TorchCraft, RFantibody, BoltzGen and Germinal, over five nanobody frameworks, with 100 designs per method per framework per target and CDR lengths fixed at 8 residues for HCDR1 and HCDR2 and 9 to 21 for HCDR3. A design passes only if it clears two thresholds: a TorchScore ipTM above 0.7 and an ESM2-150M sequence perplexity below 6.31, the second standing in as an expression proxy. Figure 3i prints the pass rates per target and Supplementary Figure S5 splits them by framework.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Section 2.3 and Figure 3i; Appendix A.4.3.2; Supplementary Table S5

summary_quotes.text: We compared TorchCraft with RFantibody, BoltzGen, and Germinal across 15 targets and five VHH frameworks 4 (Figure 3i; Supplementary Figure S5).[13, 18, 25] Designs were assessed using the joint TorchScore-confidence and ESM2-perplexity criterion described in Appendix A.4. TorchCraft achieved higher computational pass rates on many targets, with additional gains from optional AbMPNN redesign in several settings.

A VHH design passed the computational criterion only when it satisfied both a structural-confidence criterion and an expression proxy: TorchScore ipTM had to exceed 0.7, and ESM2-150M perplexity had to be below 6.31.
For each method, at each benchmark framework and for each target, 100 designs were first generated using the default settings of the corresponding method.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether a method can design nanobody CDR loops, on a fixed framework, that a structure predictor is confident bind the target and that a protein language model considers likely to express. The second part is unusual and deliberate: the pass criterion pairs a structural confidence threshold with a sequence perplexity threshold the authors calibrated against expression data. The framework-stratified figure asks a further question, how much the result depends on which of the five scaffolds is used, with the same target panel and criterion.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: No dataset and no split: a target panel. Supplementary Table S5 lists fifteen targets with a PDB entry, the target chain and residue crop and hotspot residues for each: IL13, HNMT, 1433E, BHRF1, EFNA1, CCL2, IL20, CSF1, MZB1, LIF, XIAP, RSPO1, FCGR3B, UNG and DAF, counted from its rows. Its caption fixes the CDR lengths for all designs at HCDR1 of 8 residues, HCDR2 of 8 and HCDR3 of 9 to 21. Five nanobody frameworks are used, named in Appendix A.5.2.1 as 7EOW (caplacizumab), 8Z8V (ozoralizumab), 5JDS (envafolimab), 7XL0 (vobarilizumab) and 8COH (gefurulimab), the same five identifiers that label the per-framework panels of Supplementary Figures S3 and S5. For each method, each framework and each target, 100 designs are generated with that method's default settings. The expression proxy threshold was built separately: public nanobody expression measurements were combined with accumulated TorchCraft expression data, designs expressing at least 0.08 mg were labelled high expression, and ESM2-150M perplexity was swept as a one-dimensional classifier with the threshold chosen to maximise the Matthews correlation coefficient.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: The four methods are handled differently before scoring, and the paper sets out how. For BoltzGen and RFantibody the full designed sequence is redesigned eight times with AbMPNN without fixing residues; for Germinal the original pipeline is followed, fixing CDR residues that contact the interface and applying AbMPNN only outside the CDRs. Each redesigned sequence is rebuilt to all-atom side chains with FlowPacker, the eight rebuilt models are scored with TorchScore, and the one with the highest ipTM becomes that original design's score. TorchCraft is reported raw, scored directly without redesign, and in an MPNN-polished setting where its interface CDR residues are fixed and the rest redesigned eight times with AbMPNN before the same rebuild and selection. The pass criterion is both thresholds together: TorchScore ipTM above 0.7 and ESM2-150M perplexity below 6.31. Rosetta interface-score distributions are reported separately as an additional assessment.

quotes.text: For VHH design, we compared BoltzGen, RFantibody, Germinal, and TorchCraft. For each method, at each benchmark framework and for each target, 100 designs were first generated using the default settings of the corresponding method. For BoltzGen and RFantibody, the full designed sequence was redesigned eight times with AbMPNN without fixing any residue. For Germinal, we followed the original pipeline by fixing CDR residues that contacted the target interface and applying AbMPNN redesign only to residues outside the CDR regions. Each redesigned sequence was rebuilt with FlowPacker to recover an all-atom side-chain structure. The eight rebuilt models were scored with TorchScore, and the redesign with the highest ipTM was selected as the final structure and score for that original design.

For TorchCraft, we again evaluated raw and MPNN-polished settings separately. Raw TorchCraft outputs were scored directly with TorchScore without sequence redesign. In the MPNN-polished setting, interface 23 CDR residues designed by TorchCraft were fixed and all other positions were redesigned eight times with AbMPNN. The subsequent FlowPacker rebuilding and TorchScore-based selection were identical to those used for BoltzGen, RFantibody, and Germinal.

A VHH design passed the computational criterion only when it satisfied both a structural-confidence criterion and an expression proxy: TorchScore ipTM had to exceed 0.7, and ESM2-150M perplexity had to be below 6.31.
Rosetta interface-score distributions provide an additional assessment of the predicted complexes (Supplementary Figure S3).

sections.title: What TorchScore is
sections.body: The scorer every pass rate in this panel depends on is worth stating plainly, because it is not an independent evaluator. TorchScore is a score-only loading of the same TorchFold implementation used for design: given input coordinates it skips the diffusion structure module and runs the confidence pathway, returning pLDDT, pTM and ipTM. No separate scoring network is trained, and in this study it used the pretrained AlphaFold 3 weights, the same checkpoint the designs were optimised against. Sequences rebuilt with FlowPacker are scored from those coordinates and are not refolded from sequence.

quotes.text: TorchScore is a score-only loading of the TorchFold implementation.[21] Given input coordinates, it bypasses the diffusion-based structure module and evaluates the complex through the confidence pathway, returning predictor-derived scores including pLDDT, pTM, and ipTM. No separate scoring network is trained.

In this study, TorchScore used pretrained AF3 weights, the same checkpoint used for design. Designed sequences that were rebuilt with FlowPacker were scored from the resulting coordinates; they were not refolded from sequence by TorchScore.

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: None, and none is needed in the train and test sense: no model is trained here and the panel has no labels to hold out. What the sources do describe is a dependency that runs the other way, which the authors state plainly: TorchScore uses the same pretrained AlphaFold 3 weights that TorchCraft optimised against, so the scorer is not independent of the designer.

facts.label: Organisms
facts.value: Not stated as such. The fifteen targets are named proteins with PDB entries in Supplementary Table S5, including human interleukins and an Epstein-Barr virus protein, BHRF1, but the table gives PDB entries, chains and residue ranges rather than species.

facts.label: Assays
facts.value: None in this panel. Every criterion is computed by a predictor. The paper reports wet-lab binding measurements elsewhere in the study, for minibinders and VHHs against four targets each, but those campaigns are separate from this comparison.

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: The target crop and hotspots from Supplementary Table S5, the nanobody framework sequence, which is held fixed, and the CDR length settings. The paper states that the target structures, crop regions and hotspot residues for the computational benchmarks are summarised in Supplementary Tables S2 to S6.

notes: The pass rates are printed only as figures, so no result value is recorded. The structured size is the number of targets, fifteen, counted from the rows of Supplementary Table S5; the 100 designs figure is per method, per framework and per target. The five frameworks the record's scope note lists are stated in the paper: Appendix A.5.2.1 names them as 7EOW (caplacizumab), 8Z8V (ozoralizumab), 5JDS (envafolimab), 7XL0 (vobarilizumab) and 8COH (gefurulimab), and the same five identifiers label the per-framework panels of Supplementary Figures S3 and S5. The comparison is not symmetric: BoltzGen and RFantibody get eight AbMPNN redesigns of the whole sequence, Germinal gets AbMPNN outside its interface CDRs, and raw TorchCraft is scored with no redesign at all. The paper states no licence for itself; the code repository is Apache-2.0. The same paper is the source for four other records in this batch.
